scope: Supervised typed Delay queues and actor-local leading-edge Throttle using Rust, Ouroboros and existing MCP commands.
accepted: Delay and Throttle preserve all six typed signal semantics; configured durations are 1–60000 milliseconds.
Delay captures exact values, including Hold releases and zero values, in actor-private ordered queues; Pulse(false) does not create work.
At most 16 Delay nodes, 128 queued values per actor and 256 per session; one oldest due wave per worker turn.
Scheduling anchors after accepted input/effects and rechecks original authority, target lifetime, recipients and sink scope at delivery.
Delayed admission errors that could strand old queued or held work retire the mapper and drain saved claims; retirement drops pending queues.
Throttle preserves its leading-edge window across immediate Hold releases, ignores false pulses, and never replays suppressed values.
Ouroboros Inspector duration editing and Activity queue counters share the worker model and existing MCP catalogue/state.
Accepted healthy worker state clears only worker diagnostics, preserving local errors and unrelated GUI status; stale publications cannot resurrect worker faults.

Bounded owned-native evidence covers minimum-delay timestamps, exact payloads, Hold ordering, actor-private throttle, EOF cancellation, recipient-change retirement, GUI queue/processed readings and normal shutdown.
limits: Virtual devices only, two virtual pairs, two MCP actors and three owned ordinary x64 targets; no hardware or RustDesk/global input.

Controlled-clock source tests cover capacity, injected lifetime/permission/reservation faults and mixed Timer/Delay chains; native evidence has no broad stress, process-expiry or application/device matrix.
No real-time delivery deadline, arbitrary-app compatibility, same-process or desktop-wide isolation claim.
Historical intermittent GUI stall, full Ultra/SDK/UI parity, broader device coverage and release readiness remain open; folder rename stays user-deferred.
